Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or
on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the
Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at
the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear
public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Housing
Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or
unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate
and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual
  Commissioners.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the
agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons
with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the
City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this
agenda after it has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.,
every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

SUBJECT: HOUSING ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS PROGRAM – APPROVE
  WARRANT RUN DECEMBER 15, 2024 – JANUARY 1, 2025

Background:

The Housing Authority made payments during the period of December 15, 2024, through
January 1, 2025, for a grand total of $796,810.73.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority approve check nos. 68757 – 68758 & direct
deposit voucher number 225841 reported on December 15, 2024, in the amount of
$5,406.18; and check nos. 68759 – 68793 & direct deposit voucher numbers 225842 –

   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Bethani Cardenas at ext. 5588 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: AMENDMENT TO THE SECTION 8 HOUSING CHOICE VOUCHER
  PROGRAM ADMINISTRATIVE PLAN

Background:

The Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program Administrative Plan (Plan) is a
document describing the policies that the Housing Authority Commission (Commission)
has adopted in each area where the Housing Authority (Authority) has discretion. Federal
regulations specify the policy areas that must be covered in the Plan. From time to time,
a revision is needed to reflect new regulations, United States Department of Housing and
Urban Development (HUD) guidance, or other policy changes. The Authority is
responsible for updating the Plan to include these additional elements. The plan must
also be revised whenever local circumstances require a policy change.

The recommended changes affect policies concerning the establishment of a waiting list
and selection of applicants from the waiting list. The recommended revisions change the
method of placement of applicants on the waiting list for the project-based vouchers
program  (PBV),  Soroptimist  Village,  Project Homekey  and  The  Walk
Residences. Information regarding project resident selection criteria and plans, wait list
procedures and occupancy standards have been added. Additional information was
included to define “housing readiness” as per Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority
(LAHSA) for Project Homekey.

Staff also updated online resources to the Plan, City of Norwalk Housing Profile needs,
and referenced the Norwalk Housing Authority (NHA) throughout the document instead
of Authority for clarification.
 Norwalk Housing Authority  January 21, 2025
Amendment to the Administrative Plan  Page No. 2

Additionally required updates concerning the Foster Youth Initiative Program are to
extend contracts for an additional 24 months after the 36-month initial
period. Furthermore, at the end of the term the Authority may issue a housing choice
voucher if available.

The proposed changes are summarized in the table on Attachment 1. The table also
indicates which items are discretionary changes and which are required by regulation. All
new or revised policies and regulations in the proposed Plan are shown in underline. Staff
is requesting that the Commission amend the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
Program Administrative Plan. If adopted the final Plan will be submitted to HUD.

Fiscal Impact:

There will be no impact to the General Fund. The Authority is funded solely by the United
States Department of Housing and Urban Development.

Citizens Advised:

N/A

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Norwalk Housing Authority approve the amendments to the
Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program Administrative Plan.

Page  Topic  Change
8 - 10  Introduction  Details about the references cited and the authorities mentioned in the
  administrative plan.
  A table of online resources and instructions for accessing them.
14  Profile of City of Norwalk’s Housing  The Profile of Norwalk's Housing Needs has been updated using data from the
  Needs  2024 City of Norwalk Analysis of Impediments. This includes statistics on the
  city’s population, renter households with incomes below 50% of the median
  family income, and households experiencing a cost burden of more than 50%.
20 - 21  Waiting List and Tenant Selection -  As required by statute, a Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) voucher for a
  Special Admissions  youth can only be used to provide housing assistance for a maximum of 36
  months. However, the youth may be eligible for an extension under the Fostering
  Stable Housing Opportunities (FSHO) amendments. If certain requirements are
  met, FSHO allows for an additional 24 months beyond the initial 36 months.

  In addition to providing up to 36 months of rental assistance, the Public Child
  Welfare Agency (PCWA) must offer or secure supportive services to help the
  young person on their path to self-sufficiency.

22  Waiting List and Tenant Selection  Additional information was added to define "housing readiness" according to the
  Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) for Project Homekey.
  Housing readiness means having a Coordinated Entry System (CES) score of 8
  or higher, along with all the required documentation (such as an ID, Social
  Security card, and birth certificate) entered into the Homeless Management
  Information System (HMIS).
21 - 23  Waiting List and Tenant Selection  The following projects have been included in the administrative plan:

  - Soroptimist Village: Revisions for additional units
  - Project Homekey
  - The Walk Residences

  Information about the resident selection criteria, waitlist procedures, and
  occupancy standards has also been added.
